cve_summary: The ptrace_setxregs function in arch/xtensa/kernel/ptrace.c in the Linux kernel before 3.1 does not validate user-space pointers, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory locations via a crafted PTRACE_SETXTREGS request.
commit_message:
xtensa: prevent arbitrary read in ptrace

Prevent an arbitrary kernel read.  Check the user pointer with access_ok()
before copying data in.

[akpm@linux-foundation.org: s/EIO/EFAULT/]
Signed-off-by: Dan Rosenberg <drosenberg@vsecurity.com>
Cc: Christian Zankel <chris@zankel.net>
Cc: Oleg Nesterov <oleg@redhat.com>
Cc: <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
docstring:
Summary: This function sets the extended registers for a specified child task by copying data from user space.

Parameters: 
child (struct task_struct *): The child task whose registers are to be set.  
uregs (void __user *): Pointer to the user-space structure containing the extended register values.

Returns: int: Returns 0 on success or -EFAULT if there is an error in accessing user space memory.

Logic: The function first checks if the user-provided pointer is valid for reading. If valid, it flushes and releases coprocessors if applicable, then copies the extended register values from the user space to the task's thread information and register structure. It returns an error code if any copy operation fails.
